query: Which module offers a React hook-based store factory where callers can pass their own comparison function to decide whether a selected slice of state has changed and should trigger a re-render?
why: Whole file is the equality-fn flavour of the React binding: useStoreWithEqualityFn wraps useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector with an equalityFn (L21-45), UseBoundStoreWithEqualityFn type (L47-53), and createWithEqualityFn with a defaultEqualityFn (L55-88). src/react.ts has no equality argument; subscribeWithSelector's equalityFn is for listeners, not React hooks.

query: Which store enhancer makes state updates throw an error when the code is running on the server where no browser window exists, while leaving behaviour unchanged in the browser?
why: Entire file is the experimental middleware: isSSR defaults to typeof window === 'undefined' (L13), passes config through untouched in the browser (L16-18), and replaces set/api.setState with a function that throws 'Cannot set state of Zustand store in SSR' (L19-23). src/middleware.ts only re-exports; tests/ssr.test.tsx tests server rendering, not this guard.

query: Where are the tests for saving and restoring store state through a storage backend whose reads and writes return promises, including racing restore calls, user changes made mid-restore, and migrations aborted by a newer restore?
why: Storage helper whose getItem/setItem/removeItem are async with sleep delays (L10-40); suite 'persist middleware with async configuration' (L42) covering rehydrate, migrate, merge, and the async-only races: concurrent rehydrate last-wins (L934), not overwriting user state during async hydration (L980), aborting async migration when a newer hydration starts (L1022). tests/persistSync.test.tsx uses synchronous storage and has none of the race tests.

query: Where are the type-checking tests that build a counter store with zero, one, two, three and four stacked store enhancers to make sure the combined typings still compile?
why: File is organised as counter-state specs by enhancer depth: no middleware (L40), single (L59), double (L352), triple (L532), quadruple (L635), plus explicitly annotated mutators (L769) and sliced stores (L811). tests/types.test.tsx tests core store types (setState partials, covariance, StateCreator subtyping) and only touches one middleware import.

query: Which component in the demo site draws the animated layered 3D backdrop that shifts with the mouse pointer, adds depth-of-field and vignette post-processing, and shows a still image instead if WebGL fails?
why: Experience builds six textured parallax planes that lerp toward state.pointer each frame (L20-128); Effects adds DepthOfField + Vignette (L130-148); FallbackScene renders /ogimage.jpg (L150-176); Scene switches to the fallback on canvas error (L178-191); Canvas sets up the r3f root and resize handling (L193-244). Fireflies.jsx is only the particle child and layerMaterial.js is only the shader; App.jsx just mounts Scene.

query: Which test file builds a fake in-memory implementation of a browser extension's connection API, so tests can inspect what gets sent to a mocked panel and simulate messages coming back from it, across both shared and separate connections for multiple stores?
why: File defines a Connection type wrapping a mocked subscribe/unsubscribe/send/init/error/dispatch api (L18-28), maintains namedConnections/unnamedConnections maps (L29-30), and helper accessors getNamedConnectionApis/getNamedConnectionSubscribers/getUnnamedConnectionApis/getUnnamedConnectionSubscribers/getKeyFromOptions (L37-80+) to inspect the mocked connection state per test; it is the extension-mock test harness, not the middleware implementation itself.

query: Which test file checks that state updates written as direct field mutations inside a callback still produce a properly immutable new state object, including for nested fields, while a plain object updater bypasses that mutation machinery entirely?
why: describe('immer middleware') (L6) with five cases: mutating a draft via a function updater increments count (L7-21), a non-function updater skips producing (L23-31), the replace flag swaps state entirely (L33-39), a nested draft mutation on a tags array produces a new parent object without mutating the previous one (L41-62), and the same is verified against the non-React store builder (L64-73).

query: Which test file renders a store-backed component to a string as if on a server, then hydrates that same markup on the client, and confirms no console warnings appear even when the store's state is changed while hydration is still in progress?
why: renderToString + hydrateRoot cycle (L41-63) checks text before and after hydration; the second test spies on console.error, calls setState while a hydration promise is still pending (L92-108), and asserts zero warnings were logged. Distinct from src/middleware/ssrSafe.ts, which throws on writes during SSR rather than testing React's hydration behaviour.

query: Which test file exercises the framework-independent store builder entirely outside of React, deliberately mocking React itself away, to confirm the plain store still creates, updates and reads state correctly on its own?
why: L6 vi.mock('react', () => ({})) removes any React dependency; the file inspects the exact arguments handed to the store initializer and the shape of the returned api (L13-39), then exercises get/set/increment usage directly on the vanilla store (L41+).

query: Which file in the demo procedurally generates a bundle of glowing curved light trails with randomized paths and colors and animates their shimmer over time?
why: r() randomizes a radius factor (L8); the outer component builds `count` Catmull-Rom curves from randomized points per trail, each assigned a random color (L31-59); the inner line component advances a dashOffset uniform every frame in a per-frame callback to animate the shimmer (L10-29).

query: Which file defines a custom GPU shader used by the demo's parallax background, displacing vertices over time and discarding near-transparent pixels so depth-of-field post-processing can see through the gaps?
why: A shader-material call defines a vertex shader that rotates position by a sine-driven wiggle matrix tied to a time uniform (L10-27), and a fragment shader that samples a texture and discards pixels below an alpha threshold before tonemapping/colorspace output (L28-43); the material is then registered for use as a JSX element (L45).

query: Which file assembles the demo site's page by combining the animated background, the code sample panel, a live counter and the footer links into one layout, while also owning a small counter store of its own?
why: Defines its own store with count/inc (L6-9), a local counter component reading and incrementing it (L11-19), and the top-level component laying out the animated scene, code preview, counter and details panel together (L21-36).

query: Which test file counts how many times a component actually re-renders to prove a selector-wrapping helper hands back the exact same previous result, rather than a new one, when consecutive computed values are only shallowly equal?
why: A test component invokes both the raw selector and the wrapped version on click and reports both outputs (L37-55); the suite asserts the reporting callback fires only once per interaction and that outputs stay reference-equal across rerenders whose computed values are shallowly equal (L61-119, 'returns the previously computed instance when possible').

query: Which test file confirms that an error thrown inside a selector or inside an equality-comparison function while reading from the store during render is caught by a surrounding error boundary instead of crashing the whole app?
why: Two it() blocks each define a class-based error boundary with getDerivedStateFromError (L332-347, L382+) and confirm a component whose selector throws, or whose equality function throws, triggers the boundary's fallback UI rather than an uncaught exception (L349-368, L370+).

query: Which test file compiles a single function that accepts one argument of every core exported store type together -- getter, setter, subscribe signature, listener, selector, equality function, state-creator, and bound-hook type -- purely to confirm they all still line up at compile time?
why: checkAllTypes (L71-87) takes eleven parameters each typed via a different exported type (getState/setState/subscribe off StoreApi, a StateCreator, a UseBoundStore, etc.) and is called once with matching values (L89+) purely as a compile-time compatibility smoke test; distinct from tests/middlewareTypes.test.tsx, which stacks multiple enhancers to test combined typings by depth.
